purpose: How a merchant-processing / POS agent operates the book of merchants as the durable asset: verifying how residual streams are computed and paid as mechanisms, reading merchant-level margin health and attrition signals, running honest retention and disclosed repricing, pricing support as an economic tier system, educating merchants on chargebacks without giving advice, converting the trusted-operator position into need-driven cross-sell, and deciding when the portfolio is worth holding, pruning, or selling.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator already holds a signed book of card-present local merchants (restaurants, salons, convenience stores, auto repair) acquired and deployed under one or more ISO/agent programs

residual economics (interchange pass-through, markup, split schedules, minimums, bonuses, clawbacks) are described strictly as mechanisms verified against the operator's own agreement and monthly reports, never as asserted percentages

compliance obligations touching the installed base (card-network rules, PCI-DSS revalidation, surcharging and cash-discount law, dispute-program thresholds) are jurisdiction-, network- and program-specific classes; current rules must be verified before acting
merchant underwriting, funding, reserve and termination decisions belong to the processor; the agent advocates and translates but never decides or promises outcomes
exclusions: selecting ISO/agent programs, vetting what agent agreements govern at signing, choosing merchant verticals, bundle-led selling to prospects, statement analysis as a prospecting diagnostic, and compliant claims for new-merchant acquisition - the merchant-acquisition sibling KB's territory; this KB consumes a signed agreement and a live book

POS hardware/software matching, the application/underwriting/KYC path, installation, menu and catalog build, staff training, PCI scoping at deployment, and go-live support - the deployment-and-onboarding sibling KB's territory; this KB begins after go-live

deceptive rate comparisons and guaranteed-savings promises of the form 'we will definitely save you X percent' - in saves and reviews alike, savings are verified per merchant against real statements, never asserted

stating interchange rates, markup levels, residual split percentages, or book-sale multiples as factual numbers - all appear only as mechanisms or qualitative bands verified against the governing document, report, or offer in hand

asserting card-network rule text, PCI-DSS obligations, surcharging law, or dispute-monitoring program thresholds as specifics - these are compliance classes to flag and verify currently per jurisdiction, network and processor

financial, legal, or tax advice to merchants or to the agent (including book-sale deal structuring and dispute-response legal strategy), and any merchant underwriting or funding decision, which belong to the processor and to licensed professionals

competency_questions.question: Why is the merchant book, not hardware margin, the durable asset of this business, and how does a residual actually come to exist and flow to the agent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_AS_ASSET_FRAME states why recurring residuals and their persistence outweigh one-time equipment revenue, and RESIDUAL_MECHANICS_LITERACY walks the waterfall from cardholder swipe through interchange and assessments pass-through, processor markup, and the agreement's split schedule to the agent's payout, as mechanisms with named verification documents

competency_questions.question: How do I verify that my monthly residual report is correct, and what do I do when a merchant is missing or a payout does not match the split schedule?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESIDUAL_REPORT_RECONCILIATION specifies the per-merchant tie-out against the agreement's split schedule, the discrepancy classes (missing merchant, reclassified fee item, changed schedule, clawback), and the written escalation path to the processor

competency_questions.question: How do I know whether an individual merchant is actually profitable to keep once support cost, fee mix, and volume trend are counted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MERCHANT_MARGIN_HEALTH defines net-residual-after-cost-to-serve scoring from reconciled data, and SUPPORT_ECONOMICS_MODEL supplies the per-merchant serve-cost input

competency_questions.question: How should the book be segmented so attention flows to the right merchants, and which operating numbers tell me month to month whether the book is getting stronger or weaker?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORTFOLIO_SEGMENTATION defines the tiering dimensions (margin, tenure, vertical, concentration, risk) and what each tier earns in service, and BOOK_PERFORMANCE_DASHBOARD names the monthly operating metrics (net residual trend, account attrition versus same-store volume shrink, save rate, support load, cross-sell attach)

competency_questions.question: What actually causes merchants to leave a book, and which signals warn me early enough to act?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ATTRITION_DRIVER_MAP separates the driver classes (closure, competitive rip-out, service failure, price shock, ownership change, processor termination) with which are controllable, and CHURN_EARLY_WARNING lists the leading indicators (volume decline versus seasonality, batch stops, ticket spikes, statement-shopping behavior) each mapped to a driver

competency_questions.question: How do I run a save when a competitor pitches lower rates to my merchant, without matching their deception or promising savings I cannot verify?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAVE_AND_RETENTION_PLAYBOOK sequences the rapid-response save (verify the claim against the merchant's real statement, re-anchor on delivered service, reprice only through the actual mechanism) and ETHICAL_RETENTION_BOUNDARY supplies the lines that cannot be crossed even to win the save

competency_questions.question: How do I pass through processor or network fee changes, or reprice a merchant, without triggering price-shock churn or crossing the honesty line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICING_CHANGE_GOVERNANCE distinguishes pass-through from discretionary markup change, requires disclosure before the statement lands, and ties each reprice to a per-merchant churn-risk check

competency_questions.question: Which support do I own at first call versus route to the processor or POS vendor, and what does each tier of merchant earn in response time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRST_CALL_TRIAGE_DESIGN assigns issue classes to owner (agent, processor, POS platform) with tier-based response expectations, and SUPPORT_ECONOMICS_MODEL justifies the tiers economically

competency_questions.question: How do I teach merchants to prevent and respond to chargebacks - evidence habits, descriptors, deadlines - without drifting into legal advice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHARGEBACK_EDUCATION_PROGRAM covers reason-code families as classes, prevention habits, the evidence-and-deadline response workflow, and the explicit education-not-advice boundary with referral out

competency_questions.question: What is my role when the processor holds a merchant's funds, imposes a reserve, or flags the account for excessive disputes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RISK_EVENT_SHEPHERDING defines the shepherd role (translate, document, expedite, set honest expectations) and states plainly that the decision belongs to the processor and no release or outcome may be promised

competency_questions.question: Which ongoing compliance classes must I keep flagged across the installed base, and how do I handle them without asserting rule specifics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPLIANCE_FLAG_MAINTENANCE names the recurring classes (annual PCI revalidation and non-compliance fee mechanics, surcharge and cash-discount program rules, network rule updates), each flagged as jurisdiction- and network-specific with a verify-current-rules routing, never asserted

competency_questions.question: How do I convert the trusted-operator position into cross-sell revenue without abusing the trust that created it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRUSTED_OPERATOR_POSITION explains how reliable support earns the position, ACCOUNT_REVIEW_CADENCE makes the periodic review the surface where needs are logged, and CROSS_SELL_FROM_NEED requires every offer to trace to a logged need with disclosure of the agent's economic interest

competency_questions.question: What moves the valuation of a residual book, and how do I decide between selling, holding, or pruning it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORTFOLIO_VALUATION_MECHANICS explains multiple-of-monthly-residual as a mechanism moved by attrition, concentration, vertical mix, seasoning and assignability (never quoting a market multiple as fact), and SELL_HOLD_DECISION compares offer against retained-stream scenarios under the agreement's transfer constraints with professional review flagged

competency_questions.question: What must be true operationally and contractually for a book sale to close and transition cleanly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALE_EXECUTION_AND_TRANSITION covers diligence readiness (clean residual history, attrition evidence, contract files), processor consent mechanics, non-solicit and transition-support obligations as classes, and post-close duties, with deal terms routed to professional review

glossary.definition: The recurring share of a merchant's processing economics paid to the agent each month under the agent agreement's split schedule; the unit of recurring revenue this KB manages, always verified against the monthly residual report rather than assumed.

The cost layer set by card issuers and networks that varies by card type, entry mode and merchant category; it passes through the processor and is not agent margin - quoted only from current published tables, never asserted as a fixed number.

The spread above pass-through costs where processor and agent economics live; how it is set, changed, and split is a mechanism governed by the merchant's pricing model and the agent agreement, not a standard percentage.

The exhibit of the agent agreement defining how the residual pool is computed (which fee items count, which costs deduct) and how it divides between processor and agent; the reference document every monthly reconciliation ties back to.

Two distinct erosion mechanisms: gross attrition is losing accounts outright, while same-store shrink is retained merchants processing less volume; a book can hold every logo and still bleed residual through shrink.

A mechanism by which previously paid economics (bonuses, upfront incentives, sometimes residuals) are recovered by the processor when a merchant terminates early or a condition fails; its triggers live in the agent agreement and must be modeled in save and sale decisions.

The grouping of chargeback dispute codes (fraud-type, authorization-type, processing-error-type, customer-dispute-type as classes) that determines what evidence a merchant must produce and by when; specifics vary by network and change, so current guides are always checked.

Processor risk mechanisms that delay settlement or retain a percentage of a merchant's funds when risk signals fire; imposed and released solely by the processor - the agent shepherds communication but never controls or promises the outcome.

The customary quoting convention for residual-book prices: a purchase price expressed as some number of months of current net residual; the level is a negotiated outcome moved by attrition history, concentration, mix and assignability, never a fixed market constant.

Whether the agent's residual stream and merchant relationships can be sold or transferred, and under what processor consent, notice and non-solicit conditions; set by the agent agreement and verified before any sale process starts.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for residual_book_and_portfolio_management work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix the operating frame that the book of merchants - the set of live processing accounts paying monthly residuals - is the business's durable asset, and that hardware sales, lease spiffs and activation bonuses are one-time fuel, not the engine. Every downstream decision (how hard to fight a save, what a support tier costs, whether a reprice is worth its churn risk, when to sell) is valued in book terms: expected months of retained net residual, not this month's revenue. The frame also names the asset's fragility: a residual stream exists only while the merchant processes, the agreement stays in force, and the processor keeps paying, so persistence is managed, never assumed.

included: book-first valuation of every operating decision
residual persistence as the managed quantity
excluded: how merchants are acquired or deployed - sibling-KB territory
the arithmetic of any specific residual report

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a season of book operations shows one-time revenue and residual value trading off differently than the frame assumed

pros.claim: Valuing decisions in retained-residual terms stops the operator from winning months and losing years
pros.example: declining a hardware-margin-rich lease renegotiation that would sour a salon owner whose residual stream over a normal tenure is worth far more than the box

cons.claim: A pure book-first frame can starve near-term cash the operator needs to keep running
cons.example: a solo agent skipping every upfront bonus program to maximize split, then lacking the cash to hire the installer whose service quality protects the book

failure_modes: running the book as a sales pipeline with no persistence management until attrition is visible in the payout
treating residuals as passive income and discovering at sale time that neglect priced the book down
acceptance_tests: the operator can state, for a named decision (save effort, support tier, reprice), the retained-residual value it protects or risks and why that dominates the one-time revenue at stake
revisit_triggers: the agent agreement's economics change (split, minimums, clawback terms) in a way that shifts what the book is worth per retained month
the operator's cash position forces a deliberate, time-boxed tilt toward upfront revenue

nodes.definition: Master the residual waterfall as a mechanism the operator can verify document by document, never as remembered percentages: a cardholder transaction generates interchange and network assessments that pass through at cost; the merchant's pricing model (interchange-plus, tiered, flat-rate as classes) determines what the merchant pays above that cost; the processor deducts its buy-rate or cost basis and program fees; and the agent agreement's split schedule defines which residual pool remains and how it divides. Literacy means knowing, for each layer, which document governs it (published interchange tables, the merchant's pricing agreement, the processor's fee schedule, the split exhibit) and what events move it (network updates, downgrades from entry-mode or data-quality problems, processor repricing, minimums and clawbacks).

included: the layer-by-layer waterfall and its governing documents
pricing-model classes as they shape the residual pool
excluded: quoting any rate, split or fee level as a fact
statement analysis as a sales diagnostic for prospects - acquisition-KB territory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reconciliation finds a waterfall layer behaving differently than the literacy model predicts

pros.claim: Waterfall literacy turns residual surprises from mysteries into locatable causes
pros.example: tracing a book-wide payout dip to a network assessment update passing through at cost rather than assuming the processor shaved the split

cons.claim: The mechanism is processor- and program-specific, so literacy built on one program mistranslates to another
cons.example: an operator assuming a second processor's residual pool nets out the same fee items as the first and misreading every report until the two split exhibits are compared line by line

failure_modes: reasoning about payouts from industry folklore percentages instead of the operator's own documents
missing that downgrades and non-qualified surcharges are driven by merchant-side behavior the operator could fix
acceptance_tests: for one real merchant, the operator can walk a single month from gross volume to agent payout naming the governing document at each layer and flagging which layers moved that month
revisit_triggers: a network pricing update, processor fee-schedule change, or amended split exhibit lands
a new pricing model (for example a flat-rate POS package) enters the book and changes how the pool forms

nodes.definition: Stand up the monthly discipline of tying the processor's residual report to the operator's own records before trusting a single downstream number: every live merchant appears (or its absence is explained by a documented close or move), per-merchant volume and fee lines are sanity-checked against POS and statement data, the computed split matches the agreement's schedule, and new deduction lines (program fees, clawbacks, adjustments) are identified and challenged if unexplained. Discrepancies are classed - missing merchant, reclassified fee item, changed schedule, unexplained deduction - and escalated to the processor in writing with the evidence attached, because payment errors compound silently and unclaimed corrections often have contractual time limits.

included: per-merchant tie-out against the split schedule
an auditable residual ledger over time
excluded: renegotiating the split itself - an agreement matter
merchant-facing statement explanations, which belong to the review cadence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a written escalation resolves and reveals whether the discrepancy classes and dispute-window assumptions matched the processor's actual behavior

pros.claim: A monthly tie-out catches underpayment and silent schedule changes while they are still correctable
pros.example: spotting that a taqueria's residual line vanished the month its account was migrated between processor platforms, and recovering it because the miss was raised inside the report-dispute window

cons.claim: Line-level reconciliation is tedious at book scale and tempts sampling that misses systematic errors
cons.example: checking only the ten largest merchants and missing a per-item fee reclassification that shaved every small account on the book at once

failure_modes: accepting the report total without per-merchant tie-out, so margin scoring and valuation inherit unnoticed errors
raising discrepancies by phone with no written record, leaving nothing to enforce when the dispute window closes
acceptance_tests: each month closes with every live merchant accounted for on the report or its absence explained, every discrepancy classed and escalated in writing, and the reconciled ledger updated
a sampled merchant's payout recomputes from volume and fee lines to the reported figure under the split schedule
revisit_triggers: the processor changes report format, platform, or fee-line taxonomy
a discrepancy class recurs across months, indicating a systematic rather than one-off error

nodes.definition: Score every merchant's true contribution from reconciled data: the residual the account generates, minus the cost to serve it (support time, truck rolls, supplies, chargeback handling effort), read against its volume trend and fee mix. The score surfaces the book's real shape - quiet profitable accounts that only need a yearly visit, loud accounts whose support load consumes their residual, thin flat-rate accounts whose margin never covered attention, and healthy accounts drifting toward downgrade-heavy fee mixes that invite competitive attack. Margin health is a per-merchant number with a trend, not a book average, because averages hide exactly the accounts where action matters.

included: trend over time, not point-in-time averages
excluded: deciding tier treatment - segmentation's job
fixing fee-mix problems at the merchant, which runs through the review cadence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tracked serve costs or churn outcomes show the scoring weights misranking which merchants actually deserved attention

pros.claim: Per-merchant scoring exposes the accounts where residual and effort are inverted
pros.example: finding that a mechanic shop generating a mid-sized residual absorbs more support hours than the operator's five best accounts combined, reversing its priority for renewal effort

cons.claim: Serve-cost allocation is estimation, and false precision can misrank borderline merchants
cons.example: loading one bad month of install-related tickets onto a new restaurant's score and shortlisting a normal account for culling

failure_modes: managing to the book-average margin while the bottom decile quietly consumes the top decile's residual
scoring on gross residual and never noticing which accounts cost more to hold than they pay
acceptance_tests: every merchant carries a current margin-health score built from reconciled residual and a stated serve-cost basis, with a visible trend and the inputs inspectable
revisit_triggers: support-load tracking changes how serve cost is measured
a fee-mix or volume shift moves a merchant across a score threshold

nodes.definition: Convert margin-health scores into an explicit tier structure that decides where the operator's scarce attention goes: which merchants get proactive quarterly contact, which get scheduled annual reviews, which get reactive-only service, and which enter the cull-or-fix conversation. Tiering dimensions beyond margin include tenure (seasoned accounts churn differently than first-year accounts), vertical (a restaurant's failure risk and support profile differ from a salon's), concentration (any merchant owning an outsized share of total residual is a named risk regardless of margin), and risk posture (chargeback-prone or hold-history accounts need closer watch). The tier register is the routing table every service, retention and cross-sell decision reads.

excluded: what each tier's support actually costs - the support-economics node
executing reviews or saves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retention and support outcomes show a tier's cadence over- or under-serving its merchants

pros.claim: Explicit tiers stop the loudest merchant from setting the operator's priorities
pros.example: holding a scheduled review with a quiet top-tier c-store instead of spending that afternoon on a bottom-tier account's fourth non-urgent printer complaint

cons.claim: Tiers built on last quarter's scores can lag a merchant whose situation just changed
cons.example: a reactive-tier cafe that a new competitor is actively pitching deserves top-tier attention this month regardless of its register row

failure_modes: tiering once and never re-running it, so the register fossilizes while the book moves
letting the tier label leak to merchants and insulting accounts told they are low-tier
acceptance_tests: every merchant holds exactly one tier with the assignment inputs recorded, concentration flags are set for outsized accounts, and the register states what cadence and response level each tier earns
revisit_triggers: margin-health re-scoring moves merchants across tier boundaries
a churn signal or risk event temporarily overrides a merchant's tier treatment

nodes.definition: Build the taxonomy of why merchants actually leave a processing book, with each driver tagged by controllability, because the response to churn depends entirely on its cause: business closure or owner retirement (largely uncontrollable, but predictable from volume decay); competitive rip-out by a lower-rate or free-hardware pitch (controllable through relationship and honest counter-review); service failure - unreturned calls, unresolved terminal problems (fully controllable and the most shameful loss); price shock from undisclosed fee increases (self-inflicted); ownership change where the new owner brings their own processor (partially controllable through fast new-owner engagement); and processor-initiated termination for risk (managed through shepherding, not prevented by the agent). The map also distinguishes account loss from same-store volume shrink, which erodes residual while every logo stays.

excluded: the live detection signals - early-warning's job
executing saves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a quarter of classified exits shifts the driver distribution or exposes a driver class the map lacks

pros.claim: Cause-tagged attrition turns churn from a single scary number into a set of addressable problems
pros.example: discovering that most of a year's losses were ownership changes caught late, and redirecting effort to bulk-sale-detection rather than blanket rate defense

cons.claim: Exit interviews and closure classifications are unreliable, so the map can encode flattering fictions
cons.example: logging a rip-out as 'merchant closed' because the storefront went dark two weeks after quietly switching processors and rebranding

failure_modes: treating all churn as rate-driven and answering every loss with price cuts that bleed the book's margin
ignoring same-store shrink because the account count looks stable
acceptance_tests: every closed account in the trailing period carries a driver classification with its evidence, and the distribution over drivers is reviewed rather than a single churn rate
revisit_triggers: save outcomes or post-exit evidence contradict recorded driver classifications
a new driver pattern appears, such as a POS platform's direct sales arm poaching installed merchants

nodes.definition: Wire the signals that precede departure into a watchlist the operator actually checks, because by the time an account closes the save window has usually passed: sustained volume decline beyond the merchant's seasonal pattern; batch activity stopping or thinning while the account stays open (often a competitor's terminal running alongside); a spike in support tickets or an unresolved complaint going quiet; the merchant requesting copies of statements or asking how to read fees (classic statement-shopping behavior when a rival rep has visited); news of the business listing for sale; and bank-account or ownership-detail changes. Each signal maps to its likely driver from the attrition map so the response fits the cause - a seasonality check before any panic, a service-recovery call for ticket spikes, a fast honest review for statement-shopping.

included: the watchlist and its check cadence
excluded: the save conversation itself
seasonal-adjustment modeling beyond simple per-merchant baselines

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a departure the watchlist missed, or a tuned threshold's false-alarm behavior, shows which signals carry real lead time

pros.claim: Signals bought days or weeks of lead time convert unwinnable exits into runnable saves
pros.example: catching a c-store's batches dropping to zero on Tuesdays - the day the owner's cousin's new terminal arrived - and winning the account back before the switch completed

cons.claim: Sensitive thresholds flood the operator with false alarms that dull real ones
cons.example: a snow-cone stand's every-winter volume collapse paging the watchlist annually until seasonal baselines are set per merchant

failure_modes: monitoring only account closures, which are lagging outcomes, not signals
seeing a signal and logging it without triggering the mapped response inside the save window
acceptance_tests: the watchlist runs on defined signals with per-merchant seasonal baselines, and each fired signal shows a mapped driver hypothesis and a response within the playbook's window
revisit_triggers: post-exit reviews find departures that produced no watchlist signal
false-alarm rates change after threshold or baseline tuning

nodes.definition: Codify, as identity rather than garnish, the lines the operator will not cross to keep a merchant: no fabricated or cherry-picked counter-comparisons against a competitor's pitch; no savings promises that have not been verified against the merchant's own statements; no hiding or burying fee increases hoping the merchant will not read the statement; no punitive obstruction of a merchant who has decided to leave (delayed releases, surprise exit invoices beyond the contract's disclosed terms); and extra care with small owners who do not parse statements - their trust is easiest to abuse and the abuse is the vertical's worst reputation. The boundary exists because the book's durability rests on trust: a save won by deception buys months and costs the referral network that fills the book.

included: the named forbidden tactics in saves, repricing and exits
trust as book economics, not sentiment
excluded: acquisition-stage claim compliance - the acquisition KB's territory
the mechanics of the save conversation, which the playbook sequences

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a boundary breach or a near-miss shows which pressures the codified lines fail to hold against

pros.claim: A codified boundary makes the right call fast under exactly the pressure that invites the wrong one
pros.example: a rep facing a rival's too-good-to-be-true flyer knows before the meeting that the answer is a real statement walkthrough, not a matching fiction

cons.claim: Honest saves lose some head-to-head fights against competitors willing to lie
cons.example: a merchant leaving for a teaser quote the operator refused to counter with an equally unreal number, and returning - or not - only after the first inflated statement

failure_modes: the boundary living in a document while save conversations are improvised under pressure
treating a departing merchant as an enemy and converting a clean exit into a reputation wound
acceptance_tests: sampled save and reprice conversations show verified numbers only, disclosed changes, and no forbidden tactic; departing merchants' offboarding shows no obstruction beyond disclosed contract terms
revisit_triggers: a save, reprice or exit interaction is found to have crossed a line, requiring correction with the merchant
a competitor tactic emerges that the boundary does not yet address

nodes.definition: Script the save as a sequenced play run inside the signal's window, not an improvised discount: first, respond fast - a same-week visit for a statement-shopping signal, same-day for an announced departure; second, diagnose the real driver before offering anything (a service failure is fixed with service, not price); third, verify any competitor claim against the merchant's actual statement together with the merchant - a real side-by-side on their own numbers, never a counter-flyer; fourth, re-anchor on the delivered relationship (response times, fixed problems, the bundle working); fifth, if repricing is warranted, do it through the actual mechanism with the change disclosed and durable, not a temporary teaser that resets; and last, when the merchant still leaves, exit clean - the door stays open and rip-out installs frequently disappoint. Every save and its outcome is logged against the attrition map.

excluded: prospect-stage statement analysis - acquisition territory
repricing governance rules, which the pricing node owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged save outcomes by driver class show which sequence steps actually move win-rates

pros.claim: A sequenced play stops the reflexive price cut that trains merchants to threaten departure annually
pros.example: a diner's 'your rival says I am overpaying' resolved by a joint statement walkthrough that found the rival's quote omitted its monthly fees, with no reprice given or needed

cons.claim: High-touch saves consume the operator's scarcest hours and can over-serve low-value accounts
cons.example: burning two site visits saving a bottom-tier account whose margin never justified one, while a top-tier signal aged in the queue

failure_modes: leading with a discount before diagnosing, converting a service complaint into a permanent margin cut
responding after the competitor's paperwork is signed, when the save is really a win-back at double cost
acceptance_tests: each save attempt shows a driver diagnosis before any offer, competitor claims verified on the merchant's own statement, any reprice run through the disclosed mechanism, and the outcome logged
revisit_triggers: save win-rates by driver class shift, indicating a play that has gone stale
a tier's save costs exceed the retained-residual value the tier protects

nodes.definition: Govern every price movement that reaches a merchant's statement, because undisclosed increases are the self-inflicted attrition driver: distinguish pass-throughs (network and processor cost changes the operator does not control but must still explain) from discretionary markup changes (which the operator chooses and owns); require that any discretionary change be justified per merchant against margin health and disclosed before the statement lands, in plain terms - what changes, why, and what it means on their volume; and forbid the quiet-increase pattern of padding line items no one reads. The governance also runs in reverse: when a merchant's margin can absorb it, a proactive, unprompted reduction after a cost decrease is the cheapest loyalty purchase available, and materially harder for a rival's pitch to beat.

included: per-merchant churn-risk check before any reprice
excluded: the processor's own repricing decisions
acquisition-stage pricing and proposals - sibling territory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-reprice retention outcomes show whether disclosed changes hold accounts better than the governance assumed

pros.claim: Disclosed changes convert a churn trigger into a trust deposit
pros.example: calling a salon owner before a network pass-through hits her statement, walking the change on her volume, and having her wave off a rival's 'they are raising your rates' pitch a month later

cons.claim: Full disclosure of discretionary increases invites pushback and some voluntary churn the quiet path defers
cons.example: a disclosed markup adjustment prompting two thin-margin accounts to shop, where silence would have held them another year - at the cost of the blowup when they eventually noticed

failure_modes: padding junk line items to harvest margin quietly, then losing the account and the referral relationship when a competitor's statement review exposes it
passing through cost increases with no explanation, letting the merchant assume the operator took a raise
acceptance_tests: every discretionary reprice in the trailing period shows a per-merchant justification, a churn-risk check, and a disclosure dated before the statement carrying it; pass-throughs show a plain-language explanation available to the merchant
revisit_triggers: a network or processor cost change lands that must be classified and communicated
churn attributed to price shock appears despite the governance, indicating disclosure that is not landing

nodes.definition: Treat support as a designed economic system rather than an unmeasured favor: track time and cost per merchant interaction (calls, remote fixes, site visits, supply runs), roll it into the serve-cost input of margin health, and set what each portfolio tier earns - proactive contact and fast on-site response for top-tier accounts, scheduled service for the middle, reactive-and-remote for thin accounts - so the book's best relationships are funded by design instead of whoever calls loudest. The model holds the vertical's central paradox honestly: high-touch support is simultaneously the retention engine, the trusted-operator foundation, and the margin sink, so the answer is never 'less support' in general but the right support at each tier, with automation and self-service absorbing what personal touch need not.

included: automation and self-service absorption of low-value touch
excluded: the intake and routing design - triage's job
install-phase support, which the deployment KB owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a quarter of costed interactions shows the tier service levels mispriced against the retention they buy

pros.claim: Costed support turns the loudest-caller problem into a visible allocation choice
pros.example: seeing a single bottom-tier account consume a week of monthly labor and moving it to remote-first service, freeing hours for the two top-tier restaurants that anchor the book

cons.claim: Visible service-level differences can read as unfairness if the promise was never set
cons.example: a small account that once enjoyed same-day visits calling the operator's downgrade to remote-first a betrayal because no service expectation was ever stated

failure_modes: serving all tiers identically until support hours cap the book's size and growth stalls
cutting support cost uniformly and discovering the cut hit the exact accounts whose retention pays for everything
acceptance_tests: serve cost per merchant is tracked and feeds margin health, and each tier's defined service level is actually reflected in logged interactions
revisit_triggers: support load shifts (new POS platform, new vertical mix) change per-tier costs
churn or save data shows a tier's service level under-protecting its retained residual

nodes.definition: Design the intake so every merchant issue lands with its true owner fast: the operator owns what the operator can fix - terminal swaps, connectivity, receipt and settings questions, statement explanations, supplies; the processor owns funding, holds, underwriting and account changes; the POS platform owns software defects and feature behavior. The triage matrix maps issue classes to owners with tier-based response expectations, and the operator's differentiating move is staying in the loop as the merchant's advocate on routed issues - 'I have the processor's ticket number and will chase it' - rather than dead-ending the merchant at someone else's phone tree. Escalation paths, named contacts at the processor and platform, and honest expectation-setting on what the operator cannot control are part of the design, because the small-merchant experience of processing is mostly the experience of support.

included: advocacy on routed issues and escalation contacts
excluded: go-live and installation support - deployment-KB territory
risk-event handling, which has its own shepherding node

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ticket outcomes show an issue class whose ownership mapping or response expectation is wrong in practice

pros.claim: Owned routing with follow-through converts other parties' failures into the operator's loyalty
pros.example: a mechanic whose deposit went missing remembers that the operator found it through a named processor contact in a day, not that the processor misrouted it

cons.claim: Advocacy on issues the operator cannot resolve consumes hours without control of the outcome
cons.example: chasing a platform software defect across weeks of vendor tickets for one account because the merchant expects the operator, not the vendor, to own it

failure_modes: dead-ending merchants at the processor's phone tree and teaching them the operator adds nothing after the sale
absorbing every issue personally, including ones only the processor can touch, and setting expectations that cannot be kept
acceptance_tests: sampled tickets show correct first-touch ownership, routed issues carry the external ticket reference and follow-up trail, and response times match the merchant's tier expectation
revisit_triggers: the processor or POS platform changes its support structure or contacts
ticket data shows an issue class routinely misrouted or aging past its tier expectation

nodes.definition: Run chargeback education as a standing program that makes merchants dispute-literate before their first crisis: what a chargeback is mechanically (the cardholder's bank reverses the transaction and the merchant must respond with evidence by a deadline); the reason-code families as classes - fraud-type, authorization-type, processing-error-type, customer-dispute-type - and the evidence each family wants; prevention habits wired into daily operation (clear billing descriptors so customers recognize the charge, signed tickets and delivery proof where relevant, honest refund policies that make refunding easier than disputing); and the response workflow - deadlines are short, evidence is assembled from records that must already exist, and the processor's dispute portal is where responses go. The program's hard boundary: this is education in the mechanism and the merchant's own records, never advice on a specific dispute's legal posture - contested or high-stakes cases route to the processor's dispute team and, where legal questions arise, to counsel.

included: reason-code families as classes and their evidence habits
the education-not-advice line with routing out
excluded: asserting network dispute-rule specifics or thresholds - verify current rules per network
arguing a specific dispute for the merchant

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: book-wide dispute outcomes shift after an education push, showing which habits the program actually changes

pros.claim: Merchants educated before the first dispute keep winnable disputes winnable
pros.example: a salon that adopted clear descriptors and kept signed intake forms answering its first customer-dispute chargeback inside the deadline with evidence it already had on file

cons.claim: Education is unbilled time whose payoff is invisible until a dispute that never happened
cons.example: an afternoon teaching a c-store owner descriptor hygiene shows no line-item return, and the temptation is to skip it for billable install work

failure_modes: first teaching the mechanism during a live dispute, when deadlines have consumed the options
drifting from mechanism education into advising the merchant how to fight a specific case, crossing into advice
acceptance_tests: every onboarded-to-book merchant receives the education kit with the evidence-habit checklist, and sampled dispute events show the merchant knew the deadline and where to respond
education materials carry the not-legal-advice framing and the routing for contested cases
revisit_triggers: a network revises dispute rules, codes or timelines - re-verify and refresh the materials
dispute outcomes across the book show an evidence habit the education fails to instill

nodes.definition: Define the operator's role when the processor moves against a merchant - a funding hold, an imposed reserve, entry into a dispute-monitoring program, a termination threat - as shepherd and translator, never decider: explain to the merchant in plain language what has happened mechanically and who controls it; gather and forward what the processor's risk team asks for, fast, because document latency extends holds; chase through named contacts and keep the merchant informed of real status; and set honest expectations - the operator does not control the decision, cannot promise release or timing, and says so, because a promised release that does not come destroys more trust than the hold itself. The node also covers the operator's own exposure: risk events on the book affect the operator's standing with the processor, so patterns (one vertical generating repeated holds) feed back into portfolio and education decisions.

included: honest no-promise expectation-setting and operator-standing awareness
excluded: the risk decision itself, which belongs to the processor
legal advice on a merchant's contractual remedies - route to counsel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a resolved risk event shows whether the shepherding sequence and expectation-setting held merchant trust through the hold

pros.claim: Fast, honest shepherding converts the vertical's worst merchant experience into proof of the operator's worth
pros.example: a restaurant hit with a hold before payroll had its documentation package with the risk team the same afternoon and a daily honest status call, and renewed with the operator the next year despite the ordeal

cons.claim: The shepherd absorbs anger over decisions the operator did not make and cannot reverse
cons.example: a merchant blaming the operator personally for a reserve the processor's model imposed, straining the relationship the shepherding is meant to protect

failure_modes: promising or implying a release the operator cannot deliver, converting a survivable hold into a terminal trust breach
going silent during the event because there is no good news, which merchants read as abandonment
acceptance_tests: sampled risk events show same-day merchant communication, document requests forwarded with timestamps, no promised outcomes anywhere in the trail, and a logged resolution
risk-event patterns are reviewed quarterly for portfolio and education implications
revisit_triggers: the processor changes its risk team's process, contacts or documentation expectations
a risk-event pattern concentrates in one vertical or merchant profile on the book

nodes.definition: Maintain the recurring compliance obligations that live in an installed book, as classes to flag and route rather than rules to assert: annual PCI-DSS revalidation for each merchant, including how non-validation fees arise mechanically and why helping merchants revalidate is cheaper than explaining the fee; surcharging and cash-discount programs, whose permissibility and disclosure requirements are jurisdiction-, network- and program-specific and change - every affected merchant carries a flag to verify current rules before the program starts or continues; and card-network rule updates that alter merchant obligations (descriptor standards, receipt requirements, dispute timelines), which arrive via processor bulletins the operator actually reads. The operator's stance is always the same: name the obligation class, point to the current authoritative source (processor compliance team, network documentation), and never improvise specifics from memory.

included: annual PCI revalidation operations and fee mechanics
surcharge/cash-discount program flags per jurisdiction and network
excluded: PCI scoping at deployment - the deployment KB's territory
asserting current rule text or thresholds, which must be verified per source

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule change or bulletin shows the flag inventory missing an obligation class the book carries

pros.claim: Proactive flag maintenance removes silent fee drag and program risk before merchants feel them
pros.example: a revalidation-reminder sweep clearing non-compliance fees from a dozen small accounts whose owners never knew the questionnaire existed

cons.claim: Compliance touch is unglamorous work merchants rarely credit until it lapses
cons.example: an hour walking a c-store owner through revalidation reads as bureaucracy to the merchant, though skipping it would have cost recurring fees and a risk flag

failure_modes: asserting surcharge legality from a stale memory of one state's rule and exposing the merchant in another jurisdiction
letting network bulletins pile up unread until an obligation change surfaces as book-wide fees
acceptance_tests: every merchant shows a current revalidation status and date, surcharge/cash-discount merchants carry a verify-current-rules flag with the last verification noted, and bulletin-driven obligations reach affected merchants with a dated notice
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction or network changes surcharging or disclosure rules touching flagged merchants
a processor bulletin lands with merchant-facing obligation changes

nodes.definition: Recognize and steward the position that reliable service creates: after enough fixed terminals, chased deposits and honest answers, the operator stops being 'the credit card guy' and becomes the person the merchant calls first about any technology or money-flow question - internet down, a camera quote, a lease renewal letter they do not understand. This standing is the book's compounding asset on top of the residual stream: it makes saves winnable, referrals automatic, and cross-sell conversations natural. It is also finite and fragile - built in years of showing up and spendable in one exploitative recommendation - so the node treats trust as a balance the operator draws on deliberately and only for recommendations that serve the merchant, with the operator's economic interest in any recommendation disclosed rather than discovered.

included: how service earns the first-call position
trust as a drawable, exhaustible balance
excluded: the review meeting and offer mechanics - the cadence and cross-sell nodes
acquisition-stage bundle selling to prospects

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: referral flow and save win-rates move with service metrics, showing how directly the standing tracks delivery

pros.claim: The first-call position turns the operator's book into a moat no rate sheet can attack
pros.example: a rival's lower quote dying in the trash because the mechanic calls the operator first, asks 'should I care about this?', and trusts the honest answer

cons.claim: First-call standing invites scope creep into unpaid general tech support
cons.example: the operator becoming the salon's de facto IT department for a printer that has nothing to do with processing, with no billing path for the hours

failure_modes: spending trust on a commission-led recommendation the merchant later discovers served the operator first
assuming the position exists because tenure is long, when service quality quietly decayed years ago
acceptance_tests: recommendations to merchants carry disclosed operator interest where one exists, and sampled merchants name the operator as their first call for payment and adjacent technology questions
revisit_triggers: a merchant learns of an undisclosed interest in a recommendation, requiring repair
service metrics decay in a way that erodes the standing the growth plans assume

nodes.definition: Institutionalize the periodic account review - quarterly for top-tier merchants, at least annual for the rest - as the ritual where retention actually happens: walk the merchant's recent statements in plain language (what they paid, what moved, why), preempt the competitor's favorite weapon by finding fee-mix problems first (downgrades from entry-mode habits, an untouched pricing mismatch), review chargeback and dispute trends, check equipment health and upcoming needs, confirm compliance flags (revalidation status, any surcharge-program verification), and log every need or complaint surfaced into the need-log that feeds cross-sell and service planning. The review is scheduled from the tier register, not from crisis, because the merchants who never call are where silent churn and silent cross-sell opportunity both live.

included: the review agenda and its tier-driven schedule
the need-log as the review's output
excluded: prospect statement analysis - acquisition territory
executing the cross-sell offers the need-log feeds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retention and need-log yield from completed reviews shows whether the agenda and cadence earn their hours

pros.claim: Scheduled reviews find problems while they are talking points instead of departure reasons
pros.example: a review catching a restaurant's keyed-entry drift (a new hire skipping the reader) and fixing a creeping downgrade cost before any competitor could weaponize it

cons.claim: Reviews are hours-per-merchant work that quota pressure quietly converts into sales calls
cons.example: a 'review' that opens with a camera pitch instead of the statement walkthrough teaches the merchant the meeting is a sales ambush and reviews start getting declined

failure_modes: reviewing only accounts that complain, missing the quiet majority where churn and opportunity hide
walking statements in jargon that impresses no one and clarifies nothing
acceptance_tests: review completion tracks the tier schedule, each completed review shows a statement walkthrough, compliance-flag check and a need-log entry (even if 'no needs'), and declined-review accounts are flagged as an early-warning signal
revisit_triggers: review completion rates fall below the tier schedule
churn or save data shows reviewed merchants departing anyway, meaning the agenda is missing what matters

nodes.definition: Convert the trusted position and the review need-log into additional recurring streams - but only through needs the merchant actually surfaced or the review actually found: backup internet after an outage cost a dinner rush, cameras after a break-in scare, phone service when the incumbent's renewal letter arrives, gift and loyalty programs when the merchant asks how to compete, working-capital referrals flagged as a regulated class routed to licensed providers with the operator's interest disclosed. Every offer traces to a logged need, is priced and explained with the same disclosure-first discipline as the core service, and lands as an integrated part of the one-relationship bundle rather than a bolted-on quota product. The node also owns the discipline of not offering: a merchant with no logged need gets no pitch, because the position that makes cross-sell effective is destroyed by exactly the overreach that quota logic demands.

included: the discipline of not offering absent need
excluded: designing the bundle for new-merchant acquisition - sibling territory
delivering the cross-sold services' installations, which follow their own deployment paths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: attach rate and relationship-health signals show whether need-traced discipline outperforms pushed offers over a full cycle

pros.claim: Need-traced offers close at high rates and deepen rather than spend trust
pros.example: the internet-backup offer that follows the merchant's own outage story closes itself, and the merchant thanks the operator for solving a problem they raised

cons.claim: Waiting for logged needs grows slower than quota-driven pushing, and the discipline costs revenue in any single quarter
cons.example: an operator declining to blanket-pitch cameras after a vendor spiff appears, watching a rival agent book those commissions that quarter

failure_modes: quota pressure converting reviews into ambush pitches until merchants stop taking the meeting
recommending a regulated product (capital, insurance-like offerings) directly instead of routing to licensed providers
acceptance_tests: every cross-sell offer in the trailing period traces to a need-log entry, regulated-class referrals show licensed-provider routing and disclosed interest, and no-need merchants show no pitches
revisit_triggers: attach outcomes show a need class the review agenda fails to surface
a merchant complaint or declined review indicates offer pressure is eroding the position

nodes.definition: Run the book on a small set of monthly operating numbers read together, because each alone misleads: net residual trend (reconciled, after known adjustments); account attrition and same-store volume shrink as separate lines, since a stable logo count can hide a bleeding book; save attempts, win-rate and cost by driver class; support load and serve cost by tier; cross-sell attach and the need-log conversion rate; risk-event count and open compliance flags; and concentration - the share of net residual held by the top handful of merchants. The dashboard is the operator's monthly self-review and the raw material valuation will later demand: a buyer's diligence asks precisely these trends, so the dashboard doubles as the book's continuously-maintained evidence of quality.

included: the metric set and its monthly review
excluded: the valuation computation itself
per-merchant scoring, which feeds this but lives upstream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missed book event or a diligence request reveals a gap in the metric set

pros.claim: A monthly read of paired metrics catches book decay that any single number hides
pros.example: flat account count with same-store shrink accelerating told an operator the book was weakening a full year before gross residual finally dipped

cons.claim: Dashboard upkeep competes with merchant-facing hours in a solo operation
cons.example: a month of heavy installs leaving the dashboard stale exactly when a churn cluster needed catching

failure_modes: watching gross residual alone and mistaking a bonus-inflated month for book health
tracking metrics without a monthly review ritual, so numbers exist but decisions never consult them
acceptance_tests: the dashboard updates monthly from reconciled data, shows attrition and shrink as separate trends plus concentration share, and the monthly review logs at least the decisions taken or explicitly none
revisit_triggers: a valuation or sale process requests a metric the dashboard does not maintain
a book event (churn cluster, risk pattern) that the metric set failed to surface

nodes.definition: Understand book valuation as a mechanism, never a quoted market constant: residual books trade as a multiple of current monthly net residual, and the multiple a specific book commands is moved by verifiable characteristics - attrition history (the dominant driver: a buyer prices the stream's expected decay), merchant concentration (a book living on three whales prices down for fragility), vertical and risk mix (chargeback-prone or seasonal verticals decay faster), seasoning (tenured merchants with years of stable processing outlast recent signings), margin quality (residual net of serve cost, not gross), contract assignability and processor consent (an unassignable stream is barely sellable), and the evidence trail itself (a clean reconciled ledger and dashboard history reduce the buyer's uncertainty discount). The operator's job is to know which levers their book's multiple responds to and to manage those levers years before any sale - and to state plainly that any specific multiple is a negotiated outcome verified against real offers, not a number this knowledge base can supply.

included: the multiple's driver set and their direction
evidence quality as a valuation input
managing the levers ahead of any sale
excluded: asserting any market multiple as fact
deal structuring, tax and legal terms - professional-review territory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a live offer, a peer's completed sale, or a buyer conversation shows how the levers actually priced

pros.claim: Knowing the levers converts valuation from a sale-day surprise into a managed outcome
pros.example: an operator who spent two years fixing attrition and concentration walking into a sale process with the two characteristics buyers discount hardest already repaired

cons.claim: Lever-management for an eventual buyer can distort operations that serve merchants today
cons.example: declining a fourth location of a loyal whale merchant purely to keep concentration optics clean for a hypothetical future buyer

failure_modes: planning around a folklore multiple heard at an industry event and being shocked by real offers
discovering at diligence that the agreement's assignability terms cap what any buyer will pay
acceptance_tests: the operator can rank their own book's valuation levers with current evidence for each (attrition trend, concentration share, seasoning mix, assignability status) and name which lever moves next year's value most
no valuation communication states a multiple as a market fact; offers in hand are the only priced evidence
revisit_triggers: a real offer or comparable sale provides evidence about how the levers priced
an agreement amendment changes assignability or consent mechanics

nodes.definition: Frame the sell-or-hold question as a comparison the operator actually computes rather than feels: the offer in hand (months of net residual, terms, holdbacks, earnout conditions) against the retained stream under honest attrition scenarios from the book's own history - plus the strategic positions in between: selling a segment (a distant geography, a high-support tier) while holding the core; pruning unprofitable accounts to improve the remaining book's economics; or holding through a repair period when the book's fixable levers (attrition, concentration) are temporarily depressing offers. The decision consumes the agreement's transfer constraints (consent, notice, non-solicit obligations) as hard inputs, treats clawback and holdback exposure as part of the real price, and routes deal structuring, tax consequences and legal terms to licensed professionals - the operator decides the business question, professionals paper it.

included: transfer-constraint and clawback inputs, professional routing
excluded: tax, legal and deal-structure advice - licensed-professional territory
the diligence and transition mechanics, which sale execution owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a completed or abandoned sale process shows how the modeled scenarios compared with the negotiated reality

pros.claim: Scenario comparison exposes when an impressive-sounding offer underprices the stream
pros.example: an offer quoted in months of residual that looked large until the operator's own attrition history showed the book reliably outlasting that horizon by years

cons.claim: Scenario models inherit the operator's optimism about their own attrition
cons.example: modeling the future on the book's best two years while the offer's buyer priced the worst two, and reading the honest bid as an insult

failure_modes: selling in a cash crunch at whatever is offered because the decision was never modeled before the pressure arrived
holding indefinitely by default while concentration and aging quietly erode the value a timely sale would have captured
acceptance_tests: any considered offer shows a written comparison against at least a conservative and a base retained-stream scenario built from the book's own attrition history, with transfer constraints and clawback exposure enumerated and professional review of terms documented
revisit_triggers: a credible offer arrives or the operator's liquidity needs change
the book's attrition trend or the agreement's transfer terms materially move

nodes.definition: When the decision is to sell, execute so the agreed price survives diligence and the transition: assemble the evidence room a buyer will demand - reconciled residual history, the dashboard's attrition and shrink trends, merchant contract files, the agreement's assignability provisions and the processor's consent in writing; expect and prepare for the diligence pattern where buyers re-underwrite the book merchant by merchant and discount anything undocumented; negotiate transition obligations the operator can actually deliver (introductions to key merchants, a defined support handover period) and non-solicit terms whose scope and duration the operator understands before signing; and plan the post-close reality honestly with the buyer - merchants were loyal to a person, and a botched handover triggers exactly the attrition the buyer priced against, feeding holdback and earnout clauses. Deal papers route to counsel; the operator owns making the book's operational truth match what the data room claims.

included: the data room and its evidence standards
consent, non-solicit and transition obligations as operational commitments
handover design that protects the priced attrition assumptions
excluded: legal drafting and tax structuring - counsel and professional territory
the sell/hold choice itself, decided upstream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a completed transition shows whether the handover design held post-close attrition inside the priced assumptions

pros.claim: Diligence-ready evidence defends the price the headline agreed
pros.example: a buyer's merchant-by-merchant re-underwrite finding the reconciled ledger matching processor reports for every sampled account, leaving no wedge for a late price cut

cons.claim: Transition and non-solicit obligations constrain the operator's next act in ways felt only later
cons.example: a broad non-solicit signed casually at close blocking the operator from serving a former merchant who came looking for them a year on

failure_modes: starting the data room after the offer, discovering the evidence gaps under deal-clock pressure
promising transition support the operator's next commitments cannot deliver, converting holdbacks into losses
acceptance_tests: the data room contains reconciled residual history, contract files, written processor consent and the assignability provisions before buyer diligence opens, and every transition and non-solicit commitment is one the operator has capacity-checked, with counsel review of the papers documented
revisit_triggers: buyer diligence surfaces a document class the data room lacks
post-close attrition against the transition plan triggers holdback or earnout consequences

edges.why_related: valuing the book requires understanding the mechanism that generates its residual stream
tying out a report is impossible without knowing which document governs each waterfall layer
margin scores built on unreconciled payouts inherit every reporting error
tiers are assigned from per-merchant margin scores, not gut feel about who matters
attrition is the primary threat to the asset the frame defines, so its causes are mapped against book value
each warning signal is chosen because it precedes a mapped driver, and fires with a driver hypothesis
the save play runs inside the window a fired signal opens; without signals saves become win-backs
every save move must stay inside the codified honesty lines regardless of what winning would take
the no-hidden-increase rule is the boundary applied to everything that reaches a statement
classifying a change as pass-through versus discretionary requires knowing which waterfall layer moved
service levels are designed per tier, so the tier register must exist before support is priced
triage response expectations implement the service level each tier's economics justify
dispute questions arrive through the same intake, and education routes contested cases along triage's ownership map
dispute-literate merchants generate fewer risk events, and shepherding leans on the same mechanism explanations education installed
the first-call position is earned by the routing-with-advocacy experience triage delivers
honest saves and clean exits are trust deposits the position accumulates
review frequency is scheduled from the tier register, not from who complains
the review's statement walkthrough is where disclosed changes are explained face to face
revalidation status and surcharge-program flags are standing items on the review agenda
cross-sell converts the trust balance the position holds; without the position offers are cold pitches
every offer must trace to a need-log entry, and the review is where the need-log fills
the dashboard aggregates per-merchant scores into net residual, shrink and concentration trends
the valuation levers (attrition history, concentration, margin quality) are read straight off the maintained dashboard
buyers price expected decay, and the driver mix (controllable versus not) shapes how attrition history projects forward
the sell/hold comparison prices the retained stream using the levers valuation mechanics defines
offer comparisons may only be computed from reconciled residual history, never from headline report totals
execution begins only after the modeled decision chooses sale; the data room implements a made choice
disclosure-first and no-pressure rules govern offers to existing merchants exactly as they govern saves
offers touching regulated classes (surcharge programs, capital referrals) require current-rule verification and licensed routing first
undisclosed or badly communicated repricing directly generates the price-shock attrition class
dispute-literate merchants lose less to chargebacks and fees, improving their survival and net margin
multi-service merchants are stickier, and lower attrition is the dominant lever of the book's multiple
monthly operating trends re-tier merchants whose margin, load or risk moved
logged save outcomes confirm or correct the driver classifications the map assigned
risk events reveal which merchants and habits the education program must re-target
repricing to repair a thin account's margin is also the act most likely to trigger its price-shock departure
edges.resolution_rule: margin repair proceeds only with disclosed, explained changes gated by a per-merchant churn-risk check; where disclosure would likely lose the account, the choice is between keeping it at the honest thin margin or a planned exit - never a hidden increase

edges.why_related: cutting cost-to-serve reduces exactly the high-touch contact that builds and holds the trusted position
edges.resolution_rule: protect personal touch wherever the tier's retained-residual value exceeds its serve cost; absorb reductions through automation and self-service on low-value interaction classes, never by degrading top-tier response

edges.why_related: the pressure to win a save is the exact pressure that tempts crossing the honesty lines
edges.resolution_rule: the boundary always wins: a save that requires a fabricated comparison, an unverifiable savings promise, or a hidden term is declined and the merchant is allowed to leave clean

edges.why_related: once a sale is likely, cross-sell investments whose payback exceeds the hold horizon stop making sense for the seller
edges.resolution_rule: after a sale decision, undertake only expansion commitments that transfer cleanly to the buyer and serve the merchant regardless of owner; defer operator-specific investments rather than quietly degrading service

conflict_axes.name: margin_repair_vs_price_shock_churn
conflict_axes.description: Repricing thin accounts restores book margin but undisclosed or clumsy increases are the classic self-inflicted attrition driver; the same lever heals and wounds.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reprice only through disclosed, explained changes gated by a per-merchant churn-risk check; where honest disclosure would lose the account, choose between the thin margin and a planned exit rather than a hidden increase

conflict_axes.name: high_touch_trust_vs_cost_to_serve
conflict_axes.description: Personal, fast, on-site support builds the trusted-operator position and retention, but it is the book's largest cost and caps how many merchants one operator can hold.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: differentiate by tier: fund high touch where retained-residual value justifies it, absorb the rest with automation, remote-first service and self-serve resources

conflict_axes.name: save_aggressiveness_vs_disclosure_first_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Competitors willing to lie win some head-to-head saves, and matching their fictions would win more - at the cost of the trust and referral network the book runs on.
poles: win the save at any rhetorical cost
hold the honesty boundary and lose some saves
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the boundary is absolute: verify claims on the merchant's own statement, never counter-fabricate; accept that some deception-won departures return after the first inflated statement

conflict_axes.name: sell_for_liquidity_vs_hold_for_compounding
conflict_axes.description: A book sale converts years of future residual into cash today; holding compounds the stream and the cross-sell position but carries attrition, concentration and processor risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide from the modeled comparison of offer versus retained-stream scenarios built on the book's own attrition history, with transfer constraints and clawback exposure priced in and professional review of terms

conflict_axes.name: keep_every_account_vs_prune_unprofitable_tail
conflict_axes.description: Every account adds gross residual and book size, but the unprofitable tail consumes support hours and drags the margin quality buyers and the operator's economics both price.
poles: cull accounts that cost more than they pay
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fix before firing: re-tier service, correct fee mix, or reprice with disclosure; exit only accounts that stay uneconomic after the fixes, and exit them cleanly

conflict_axes.name: cross_sell_monetization_vs_trusted_position_preservation
conflict_axes.description: The trusted-operator position makes cross-sell effective, and every quota-driven or undisclosed-interest offer spends the exact trust that made it effective.
poles: protect the position from offer pressure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offers trace to logged needs, interests are disclosed, regulated classes route to licensed providers, and merchants with no logged need receive no pitch

conflict_axes.name: merchant_advocacy_vs_processor_decision_authority
conflict_axes.description: The operator advocates hard for merchants in holds, reserves and risk flags, but the decision belongs to the processor - and overpromising advocacy outcomes destroys the trust advocacy builds.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: advocate through speed, documentation and named contacts while stating plainly that release and timing are the processor's call; never promise an outcome

conflict_axes.name: education_depth_vs_advice_boundary
conflict_axes.description: Deep chargeback and compliance education serves merchants, but the more specific the guidance, the closer it drifts to legal or financial advice the operator must not give.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: teach mechanisms, classes and the merchant's own records; route specific contested cases, legal questions and regulated products to the processor's specialists and licensed professionals

conflict_axes.name: whale_concentration_income_vs_portfolio_resilience
conflict_axes.description: A few large merchants can carry a book's residual, and their weight simultaneously creates the concentration that discounts valuation and makes any single departure existential.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: serve whales at the highest tier while tracking concentration share on the dashboard; when share crosses the operator's comfort line, grow the base rather than declining whale business

edge_cases.description: A live merchant simply does not appear on the monthly residual report
edge_cases.trigger: platform migration, account reclassification, or a reporting error drops a paying account from the payout
edge_cases.mitigation: the tie-out flags the absence the same month; verify the merchant is still processing, then escalate in writing with volume evidence inside the report-dispute window

edge_cases.description: The processor reclassifies a fee item so the residual pool nets out smaller across the whole book
edge_cases.trigger: a fee-schedule or split-exhibit change alters which lines feed the pool
edge_cases.mitigation: compare the report's pool computation against the governing split schedule line by line, request the change documentation, and challenge any deduction the agreement does not authorize

edge_cases.description: A profitable restaurant is hit with a funding hold days before its payroll
edge_cases.trigger: a risk model flags a large batch, a dispute spike, or a processing-pattern change
edge_cases.mitigation: same-day plain-language explanation, immediate document shepherding to the risk team, daily honest status updates, and no promised release date at any point

edge_cases.description: A competitor shows the merchant a cherry-picked comparison flyer claiming they are overpaying
edge_cases.trigger: statement-shopping signal or the merchant asks about a rival's savings claim
edge_cases.mitigation: run the joint walkthrough on the merchant's real statement, surface what the flyer omits (monthly fees, teaser resets), and decline to counter with any unverifiable number

edge_cases.description: A seasonal merchant's volume collapse fires churn alarms every year
edge_cases.trigger: the watchlist lacks a per-merchant seasonal baseline
edge_cases.mitigation: set seasonal baselines per merchant so alarms fire on deviation from the merchant's own pattern, not from a flat threshold

edge_cases.description: A merchant's dispute count approaches a network monitoring-program threshold
edge_cases.trigger: a chargeback spike from fraud, descriptor confusion, or a fulfillment problem
edge_cases.mitigation: immediate re-education on the driving reason-code family, fix the operational cause, and coordinate with the processor on the program's current requirements rather than asserting thresholds from memory

edge_cases.description: The business sells and the new owner keeps the POS but the processing agreement does not transfer
edge_cases.trigger: an ownership change discovered late, often via a changed bank account or a new signer's voice on support calls
edge_cases.mitigation: treat ownership-change signals as a top-priority alarm; engage the new owner immediately, and route them into a new application fast since underwriting a new entity is the processor's requirement, not optional

edge_cases.description: A whale merchant holding an outsized share of net residual threatens to leave
edge_cases.trigger: a competitor targets the book's largest account, or the whale's own economics tighten
edge_cases.mitigation: run the full save play at top priority but inside the honesty boundary and without panic pricing that breaks book economics; treat the episode as confirmation to grow the base and re-check concentration

edge_cases.description: A surcharge or cash-discount merchant operates under rules that changed since the program started
edge_cases.trigger: a jurisdiction or card network updates surcharging or disclosure requirements
edge_cases.mitigation: the standing verify-current-rules flag fires; confirm the current requirements through the processor's compliance channel and adjust or pause the program before it draws penalties

edge_cases.description: A merchant's annual PCI revalidation lapses and non-compliance fees begin accruing
edge_cases.trigger: the questionnaire deadline passes unnoticed by an owner who never knew it existed
edge_cases.mitigation: run a revalidation-reminder sweep ahead of deadlines, walk lapsed merchants through the questionnaire, and explain the fee mechanism honestly rather than letting it read as a junk charge

edge_cases.description: A book buyer's diligence demands residual history and contract files the operator never maintained
edge_cases.trigger: a sale process starts before the data room exists
edge_cases.mitigation: maintain the reconciled ledger, dashboard history and contract files continuously so diligence readiness is a byproduct of operations, not a deal-clock scramble; undocumented claims price as discounts

edge_cases.description: An account quietly splits its volume, running a competitor's terminal alongside the operator's
edge_cases.trigger: batches thin on specific days or card types while the account stays open
edge_cases.mitigation: treat partial-volume loss as active churn in progress: visit, diagnose which offer pulled the split volume, and either win it back honestly or plan for the full departure it usually precedes

workflow.description: State that decisions are valued in retained net residual and that persistence is managed, not assumed
workflow.gate: a named decision class (save, tier, reprice, sell) is expressed in retained-residual terms with the one-time/recurring distinction explicit
